solves: Shows who the person is, by the photo or, without a photo, by the person icon, in a square with rounded corners and a border drawn over the photo.
use_when: Next to a person's name, when the person needs to be recognized in a list, a field or a header.
sm next to body text, in a list and in the select; md in a header, card and table row; lg in a profile.
Without a photo, keep the avatar: it draws the person icon whenever there is no src or the image does not load.
Put the person's name next to it: the avatar alone does not identify anyone with certainty.
Use the same size for every avatar in a list.
do_not_use_when: As a button: the avatar receives no click and no focus.
As an action icon: use nph-icon.
As a circle: the avatar is a square with rounded corners, and there is no shape property.
With an empty frame: leave src out and the person icon shows.

size.constraint: The Figma property size. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the box by it. The frame is 24, 32 or 40 px. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

src.constraint: The address of the photo. The Figma property `tipo` is not a property in code: it derives from src, with a present src as `foto` and no src as `sem foto`. Empty or whitespace-only counts as no src. The photo takes the place of the person icon on load, a failed photo leaves the icon, and a new src starts the wait again. No event is emitted. The name is a technical proposal of P74.

label.constraint: The accessible name. With text, the host takes role img and aria-label. Empty or whitespace-only, the host takes aria-hidden true. Without label is valid and silent, with no console.error. The name is a technical proposal of P74.

size.choose_when: sm next to body text, in a list and in the select; md in a header, card and table row; lg in a profile and person highlight.

type.choose_when: With src when the person has an image; without src when there is none, and the person icon shows. It is not a property: it derives from src.

default.changes_for_user: A square frame with the photo, or with the person icon in color/muted-foreground; the border border/width in color/border stays over the photo. It has no state of its own.

business_rules: The avatar has no state of its own: no hover, no focus, no disabled and no animation.
The frame is never empty: without a photo, while the photo loads and when it fails, the person icon shows.
The frame is a square with rounded corners, never a circle, and there is no shape property.
The border is drawn by the avatar inside the frame and over the photo; it keeps overlapped avatars apart.
The name is next to the avatar: leave label out and the avatar is hidden from the screen reader; alone, pass label with the person's name.
ai_hints: Use nph-avatar next to a person's name, so the person is recognized faster; for an action icon, use nph-icon.
Pass src when the person has a photo and leave it out when there is none: the person icon shows, and the frame is never empty.
Leave label out when the name is next to the avatar, because the avatar is then hidden from the screen reader; alone, pass label with the person's name.
Choose the size by the place: sm next to body text and in a list, md in a header and card, lg in a profile; use the same size for every avatar in a list.
Do not use it as a button: the avatar receives no click and no focus.
To hold the place of an avatar while a list loads, use nph-skeleton with the avatar shape of the same size.

accessibility.semantics: An image on the host, or nothing. Without label, aria-hidden true and no role. With label, role img and aria-label on the host. The inner image has an empty alt. The avatar is never focusable and is not a button.
accessibility.accessible_name: The label, when it has text. With the person's name next to the avatar, label stays out and the avatar is hidden from the screen reader.
accessibility.focus: The piece does not receive focus and has no tabindex. Inside a control, the focus belongs to the control.
accessibility.contrast: The person icon, color/muted-foreground on color/muted, passes 3:1 in light and dark, in every brand; nph-avatar.test.ts measures it by hand until the accessibility gate of P72 arrives. The photo is the person's image and is not measured.
accessibility.color_alternative: The avatar does not communicate state, so there is nothing to tell apart by color.

invalid_combinations: A size outside sm, md and lg — the piece draws nothing.
A circle or any other shape — the frame is a square with rounded corners and there is no shape property.
Initials in place of the person icon — the avatar has no initials.
anti_patterns: Using the avatar as a button.
Using the avatar as an action icon.
Using different sizes for the avatars of one list.
Using the avatar alone to identify a person, without the name.

sources.design_md: design.md, avatar/size-*, avatar/radius-*, color/muted, color/muted-foreground, color/border, border/width and icon/size-*
sources.decision: P74 — API and semantics of nph-avatar, 20-10-2026
sources.usage_evidence: none in code yet; nph-select (DSA-29) will take it at the start of the trigger and of the option, and nph-avatar-stack (DSA-25) will overlap a group of them
